definition: First flagellomere, the first long segment of the antenna after scape and pedicel. Older keys number antennal segments from the scape, so 'antenna 3' = f1, 'antenna 4' = f2, 'antenna 5' = f3. Lengths and ratios to the labrum are used in many couplets.

Hyaline sensory rod on the flagellomeres. Number per segment (antennal formula), length relative to the segment (e.g. asc/f2) and presence of spurs are diagnostic (e.g. S. gemmea and S. raynali have spurred ascoids).
Small sensillum on the flagellomeres. Its presence on antenna 5 (f3) separates P. argentipes from P. philippinensis in Lewis 1978.

synonyms: Newstead's spines; Newstead scales; hyaline sensilla; peg sensilla
definition: Club-shaped sensilla on palpal segment 3 (sometimes 2). Their arrangement is used by Quate 1962 and Lewis 1978.
The sequence of palp segments from shortest to longest, e.g. 1-2-4-3-5.
The dorsal mouthpart. Its length is the standard against which antenna 3 and wing length are compared.
The chamber behind the mouthparts. Its armature (teeth, sclerotized area, arch) is the most-used character in female Sergentomyia keys.

synonyms: Horizontal teeth; cibarial teeth; main teeth
definition: The main transverse row of teeth at the hind end of the cibarium. Counts and row shape (concave, convex, straight) are key characters.
Smaller teeth in one or more rows in front of the hind teeth. Number of rows (e.g. 'three rows of fore teeth') is used in Neophlebotomus couplets.

synonyms: Pigmented area; pigment belt; plage pigmentée
definition: Darkened area of the cibarium in front of the tooth row. Its shape (bifid tip, anterior projection, narrow/linear) is diagnostic.
Arched sclerite at the front of the cibarium; the distance between arch and teeth is used in Lewis 1978 couplet 168.
A median notch at the hind end of the cibarial ventral plate; characteristic of the S. babu series.
Tube behind the cibarium. The hind part may carry an armature of teeth, scales, ridges or spicules, which is key for Phlebotomus subgenera and Parrotomyia.
The teeth, scales or ridges lining the hind part of the pharynx.
Ratio of the length of vein section R2 (alpha) to R2+3 (beta). 'R1 overlap' is the distance by which the tip of R1 passes the fork of R2+3.
In Phlebotomus the hairs on tergites 2-6 are erect and arise from large sockets; in Sergentomyia they are recumbent with small sockets. This is couplet 1 of most keys.
Paired sperm-storage organ. Segmented (ringed), striated, smooth capsule or tubular forms define subgenera.
The apical part of the spermatheca, sometimes on a narrow neck.
Each spermatheca opens into an individual duct; these join into a common duct. Their lengths separate P. shadenae, P. stantoni and P. hoepplii.
Sclerite of the female genital chamber.
Basal segment of the male clasper. Its basal process or tuft of hairs (brush) is diagnostic.
Distal segment of the clasper. Number and position of its spines (terminal, subterminal, near middle) are used at genus and subgenus level; Sergentomyia has an accessory seta.
Fine seta on the gonostyle of Sergentomyia (absent in Phlebotomus).
Middle appendage of the male genitalia. Number of lobes (simple, bilobed, trilobed) separates Euphlebotomus and Anaphlebotomus species.
The sclerotized sheath through which the genital filaments emerge (older keys call it the aedeagus). Its tip shape is used in Parrotomyia and Larroussius.

synonyms: Genital filaments; ejaculatory ducts; penal filaments
definition: Paired ducts leaving the sperm pump. Their length relative to the pump is diagnostic (e.g. P. shadenae versus P. stantoni).
Internal pump that the genital filaments leave. Used as the unit for filament length.
Lobe beside the gonocoxite. Terminal spines on it occur in subgenus Phlebotomus.
Paired rods next to the sperm pump; characteristic of Idiophlebotomus.
Scales on the anepimeron (thorax side); counted in the Lewis 1987 Grassomyia key.
